messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Replace the person in the video with the person shown in the reference photo. Use the reference photo only to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body, while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please replace the person in the video with the person shown in the reference photo. Only use the reference photo to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body, while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands still and then walks slowly forward toward the camera.","camera":"A low-angle, full-body shot that remains static as the character approaches.","clothing":"A brown and orange plaid three-piece suit with a white dress shirt and a dark tie.","hair_color":"Black.","hairstyle":"Short, dark hair with a flat-top style.","identity":"A 3D-rendered male character with dark skin, a short beard, and a slim build.","scene":"An outdoor paved area under a concrete overpass, with road signs and barriers in the background."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The character's face and visible hands became noticeably darker, matching a darker skin tone. The original hairstyle, black hair, plaid three-piece suit, white shirt, dark tie, walking action, overpass scene, and low-angle camera framing remain essentially the same.
arguments.requested_change: Replace the person with the reference person's facial identity and skin tone, applying the skin tone consistently to face and body while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.
uncertain: Whether the facial identity was accurately replaced with the reference person's identity, not just the skin tone.
unexpected_changes: The reference person's white hair was not applied, consistent with the instruction to retain the current hairstyle and hair color, but the facial identity match remains difficult to verify.
